summary: Jesus calls Himself the true vine and His disciples the branches, urges them to abide in Him and love one another, and warns that the world will hate them.
key_insight: Jesus does not command the branches to produce fruit. He commands, “Abide in Me.” Fruit is what grows on a branch that stays joined to the vine: “without Me you can do nothing.” And the Father’s pruning is given to branches that are already bearing fruit, so that they will bear more.
story: “I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinedresser.” Every branch in Him that bears no fruit, the Father takes away; every branch that bears fruit, He prunes, so that it will bear more. The disciples were already clean because of the word He had spoken to them.

“Abide in Me, and I in you.” A branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, and neither could they unless they remained in Him. “I am the vine, you are the branches. He who abides in Me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without Me you can do nothing.” Whoever does not abide is thrown out like a branch and withers, and such branches are gathered and burned. But if they abide in Him and His words abide in them, they will ask what they desire, and it will be done. The Father is glorified when they bear much fruit.

“As the Father loved Me, I also have loved you; abide in My love.” They would remain in His love by keeping His commandments, just as He had kept His Father’s commandments and remained in His love. He told them this so that His joy might remain in them, “and that your joy may be full.”

“This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one’s life for his friends.” They were His friends if they did what He commanded. He no longer called them servants, because a servant does not know what his master is doing; He had made known to them everything He heard from His Father. “You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain.”

“If the world hates you, you know that it hated Me before it hated you.” They did not belong to the world; He had chosen them out of it, and so the world would hate them. A servant is not greater than his master: if people persecuted Him, they would persecute them too. Whoever hated Him hated His Father also, and so the word written in their law was fulfilled: “They hated Me without a cause.”

“But when the Helper comes, whom I shall send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will testify of Me.” And they too would bear witness, because they had been with Him from the beginning.

scene.label: Israel the vine
scene.text: The prophets pictured Israel as God’s vine, brought out of Egypt and planted in the land (Psalm 80:8), but a vine that yielded wild grapes (Isaiah 5:1–7; Jeremiah 2:21). The emblem was still before every pilgrim’s eyes: Josephus describes a great golden vine with hanging clusters above the entrance to the temple sanctuary. Jesus calls Himself the “true” vine: in Him God has the fruitful vine He looked for.

scene.label: Pruning and burning
scene.text: Vinedressers cut vines back hard and pinched off extra shoots so the plant’s strength went into fruit, not leaves. Vine wood was too soft to build with; Ezekiel asked whether anyone could make even a peg from it (Ezekiel 15:3). A branch that bore no fruit was good only for the fire.

scene.label: Friends
scene.text: In the Old Testament, Abraham is called God’s friend, and the LORD spoke to Moses “as a man speaks to his friend” (Isaiah 41:8; Exodus 33:11). Jesus gives that title to the eleven, and grounds it in what He has shared with them: everything He heard from the Father.

scene.label: Without a cause
scene.text: The line comes from psalms of David’s suffering (Psalm 35:19; 69:4). King David’s enemies hated him for no reason; so would the Son of David’s.

witnesses.john: Only John records the vine, the last of Jesus’ “I am” sayings with a picture. It turns the promises of chapter 14 into a way of life: abide in Him, bear fruit, love one another, and expect the world’s hostility. “Abide” runs all through this chapter and becomes a key word of John’s first letter (1 John 2:6, 24–28).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the true vine, the source of all life and fruit for His people. He loves them as the Father loves Him, calls them friends, and chose them before they ever chose Him.
seeing.living: Fruit does not come from straining but from staying: let His words remain in you, and pray from them. When the Father’s pruning hurts, remember that He prunes branches that are bearing fruit. And when the world turns cold toward you, remember that it hated Him first.
seeing.ponder: What is the Father pruning in your life right now, and are you staying close to the Vine while He does it?

preaching.big_idea: Branches do not strain to bear fruit; they abide in the Vine.
preaching.watch_for: “Abide” runs through verses 4–10 like a refrain. Then at verse 18 the chapter turns from abiding in His love to facing the world’s hatred: the same union with Jesus that bears fruit also brings His rejection.
